note: The two original skills (`why-notes` recorder and `consult-why-notes` lookup) were collapsed into a single `why-notes` skill with two entry-point scripts (`record.py`, `consult.py`) sharing a `note.py` module. The trigger was the class-structure ask in #6: a shared Note/NotesStore cannot live cleanly across two sibling skill directories without breaking skill self-containment, and vendoring the module into each skill would drift. Considered alternatives: (1) sibling shared package imported via sys.path — fragile when skills are vendored individually; (2) keep two skills, copy the module — defeats the point. Single skill with multiple entry scripts gives trivial code sharing while SKILL.md still describes two distinct triggers (record on rationale, consult before edits). The `b7a9d15b` precedent (named helpers, not inline main) is what this generalizes — one step further to classes when duplication crosses module boundaries.
